title: Testing Statistical Dependence in Labeled Graphs under Mismatches

problem.claim: Determine whether two labeled graphs or subgraphs exhibit statistical dependence.

gap.claim: Classical dependence testing does not directly address dependence expressed through structural similarity, label correlation, or their interaction in graphs, especially under imperfect or noisy node alignments.

contributions.claim: A practical dependence-testing framework for labeled graphs based on mutual information over a structure-weighted joint label distribution.
The framework jointly captures topological and attribute-based signals and is designed to remain robust to imperfect or noisy node alignments.
The work provides theoretical guarantees with explicit error bounds.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their dependence-testing framework as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method was validated on synthetic and real-world datasets, including lipocalin protein structures and recurring motifs in the Cora citation network.
The authors report that the proposed test is statistically sound and effective for uncovering nontrivial dependencies in graph data.

narrative_sequence.summary: Labeled graphs represent systems in which topology and node attributes both carry important information.
A central analytical task is testing statistical dependence between graphs or subgraphs.
Graph dependence may arise from structural similarity, label correlation, or their interaction, creating challenges beyond classical testing.
The authors propose a mutual-information framework using a structure-weighted joint label distribution that is intended to handle noisy alignments.
The abstract reports theoretical error bounds and validation on synthetic and real-world graph datasets.

source_observation.claim: The proposed test combines structural and label information through a structure-weighted joint label distribution.

interpretation.claim: Dependence tests for attributed relational data may need a joint representation that preserves both topology and attributes.

application.claim: When analyzing dependence in labeled graphs, consider integrating structural weighting with label-based mutual information.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how the approach behaves outside the reported graph settings or under specific alignment-error regimes.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact test statistic, algorithm, or computational complexity.
The abstract does not report dataset sizes, baseline comparisons, numerical results, or the explicit error bounds.
The abstract does not detail the assumptions required for the theoretical guarantees or robustness to node misalignment.
